decisions.reason: Designs paste_image.png / paste_file.ext with (2),(3) appended before the extension, reserves names within the batch by inserting each chosen name into the taken set immediately, scopes renaming to the paste source (drop and picker keep real names via item.source tagging or renaming in the paste handler), and explicitly reserves across live snapshot occurrences. Extension/MIME and chip/upload details are present but marked unscored guidance.

Names the live composer snapshot occurrences (input.state.getSnapshot() filtered to SOURCE) plus current-batch items as the authoritative taken-name source, and explains that the records alive-subscription (plugin-attachment-flow.js) deletes the Map entry on any momentary empty snapshot while the attachment is still rendered live, so the cache would wrongly free the name. The records Map is demoted to a render-cache/supplement.

Grounds the diagnosis in the captured response (x-cache: HIT, age 178, stale list topped by v0.2.9) and renderCurrentChip(tag) rendering the fetched tag when semverCmp is <= 0. Gives the semantic rule: show the update chip only when fetched > running PLUGIN_VERSION, otherwise display the running version, never an older fetched tag.

Proposes concrete tests: consecutive paste batches yield paste_image.png then paste_image(2).png; a momentary empty snapshot retiring the records entry still blocks the name from live state; drop/picker keep original paths verbatim; chip tests mock the stale v0.2.9 fetch against PLUGIN_VERSION 0.2.10 (assert green chip shows v0.2.10, never v0.2.9) and a newer v0.2.11 showing the update chip.

Requires keeping the hand-inlined PLUGIN_VERSION in lib/client.js in sync with package.json, running node --check on the shipped lib bundle plus behavioral regressions, and explains there is no host-side update endpoint: users receive the new artifact by fetching it on next page load with a hard refresh, the tag/chip alone installing nothing.
